messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you sell your acoustic guitar quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Research the Market** | • Look up similar models on eBay, Reverb, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds.
• Check recent sales prices, not just listings. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively and avoid over‑ or under‑pricing. | | **2. Clean & Tune** | • Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body).
• Replace old strings if needed and tune it to standard pitch (E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E). | A well‑tuned, clean instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **3. Take High‑Quality Photos** | • Capture the front, back, sides, headstock, neck, and any unique features.
• Include close‑ups of any wear, scratches, or repairs. | Good photos reduce buyer questions and increase trust. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | • Model, year, brand, wood type, finish, condition, any modifications, and why you’re selling.
• Mention any included accessories (case, strap, picks). | Transparency builds confidence and reduces post‑sale disputes. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform** | • **Online marketplaces**: eBay, Reverb, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, OfferUp.
• **Local music stores**: Many accept used gear for cash or store credit.
• **Consignment shops**: They handle marketing and sales but take a commission.
• **Forums & communities**: Gearslutz, Reddit r/Guitar, local Facebook groups. | Each platform has pros/cons: eBay offers wide reach but fees; local stores offer instant cash; consignment shops reduce effort but cost a cut. | | **6. Set a Realistic Price** | • Use the research from Step 1 as a baseline.
• Add a small margin for negotiation (e.g., $50–$100 above the lowest recent sale). | Buyers expect to haggle; setting a slightly higher “asking” price gives room to negotiate. | | **7. Draft a Safe Transaction Plan** | • Decide whether you’ll ship or meet locally.
• If shipping: use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and insured USPS Priority Mail or UPS Ground.
• If local: meet in a public place (coffee shop, police station) and bring a friend if possible. | Safety and protection against loss or damage are paramount. | | **8. Handle Payment Securely** | • For local sales: cash or Venmo (if you trust the buyer).
• For online sales: PayPal Goods & Services, or a bank transfer. | Avoid scams by using secure payment methods that offer buyer/seller protection. | | **9. Finalize the Sale** | • Sign a simple bill of sale (include serial number, condition, price, date, and both parties’ signatures).
• Keep a copy for your records. | A bill of sale protects both parties and can be useful for tax purposes. | | **10. Ship or Deliver** | • Package carefully, label clearly, and track the shipment.
• If delivering, confirm the buyer’s identity and keep a record of the hand‑off. | Proper packaging and tracking reduce disputes and protect against loss. | ### Quick Tips | Tip | How to Apply | |-----|--------------| | **Use a tuner** | Before listing, tune the guitar to standard E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E. A well‑tuned instrument looks more professional. | | **Highlight unique features** | If your guitar has a custom finish, inlay, or special hardware, mention it. | | **Offer a return policy** | A short return window (e.g., 7 days) can reassure buyers and boost sales. | | **Be responsive** | Answer questions promptly; quick replies often lead to faster sales. | | **Check local regulations** | Some cities require a sales tax receipt or have specific rules for instrument sales. | --- #### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2010 Martin D-28 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition – $1,200 Description: - 2010 Martin D-28, natural finish, mahogany back & sides, spruce top. - Serial #12345678, no visible damage, minor fret wear. - New strings installed, tuned to standard E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E. - Comes with a hard case, strap, and pick. - Reason for sale: upgrading to a 12‑string. Photos: Front, back, headstock, neck, case, close‑up of fretboard. Price: $1,200 (negotiable within $50). Shipping: Will ship via UPS Ground, insured, with tracking. Local pickup available in [City]. Payment: PayPal Goods & Services preferred. ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your chosen platform. Good luck with your sale!
